generic_name: Niraparib Tosylate Monohydrate and Abiraterone Acetate
drug_class: PARP Inhibitor combined with Androgen Biosynthesis Inhibitor
purpose: This medicine is used to treat adults with prostate cancer that has spread to other parts of the body and has certain genetic mutations called BRCA. It is used along with a steroid called prednisone or methylprednisolone. It helps slow down or stop the growth of cancer cells.
how_it_works: This medicine is actually two drugs working together. Abiraterone blocks your body from making testosterone, which prostate cancer cells need to grow. Niraparib targets and damages cancer cells by blocking a protein called PARP that cancer cells rely on to repair themselves, which causes the cancer cells to die.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include fatigue or tiredness, joint or muscle pain, nausea, constipation, high blood pressure, low red or white blood cell counts, swelling in the legs or feet, hot flashes, and low potassium levels. Let your doctor know if any of these bother you.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious drops in blood cell counts, high blood pressure, liver problems, and heart problems. It should never be taken by women who are pregnant or may become pregnant as it can harm an unborn baby. Men should use effective birth control during treatment. You must take it with prednisone or methylprednisolone exactly as prescribed. Regular blood tests to monitor your blood counts and liver are very important.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 2 tablets taken by mouth once a day on an empty stomach (at least 2 hours after eating and 1 hour before eating again). Each tablet contains niraparib 100 mg and abiraterone 500 mg, so you take 2 tablets together. Always take it with your prescribed steroid as directed by your doctor.
